svg.data-integrated-interfaces: 2 x QSFP-DD, 6 x QSFP28, 16 x SFP28, 24 x SFP+
svg.data-slices: 2 (slice 0 colour-coded blue, slice 1 purple); port mode is set per slice
svg.data-port-modes-sfp28: 25GbE and 10GbE dual-rate - data sheet Table 2, "16 SFP28 dual-rate ports capable of 25Gb and 10Gb Ethernet". Cisco publishes no per-optic list for this chassis and points at the Cisco Optics Compatibility Matrix, so this is the rate list and not an optics list
svg.data-port-modes-sfp-plus: 10GbE LAN and WAN (OTN) - data sheet Table 2, "24 SFP+ ports capable of 10Gb Ethernet (LAN) and WAN (OTN)". Configuration guide Table 41 adds 1GbE and 5x1GE_5x10GE slice modes from IOS XR 7.9.1
svg.data-port-modes-qsfp28: 10, 40 and 100 Gigabit Ethernet - data sheet Table 2, "6 QSFP28 ports capable of 10Gb, 40Gb, and 100Gb Ethernet". The 40G port mode needs IOS XR 7.8.x or higher
svg.data-port-modes-qsfp-dd: 10, 40 and 100 Gigabit Ethernet on the cage - data sheet Table 2, "2 QSFP-DD ports capable of 10Gb, 40Gb, and 100Gb Ethernet" - plus 1x100G transponder mode with a 400G digital coherent module, per Table 19 of the configuration guide, which lists ASR-9902 ports 11 and 37 and marks the 400G and muxponder modes No
svg.data-power-input-ac: 200-240 VAC high line, 90-130 VAC low line, 50-60 Hz
svg.data-power-input-dc: -48 VDC nominal, -40.5 to -72 VDC, 40 A max per module
svg.data-fixed-board-allocation-w: 614 W allocated to 0/0 ASR-9902-LC in the install guide's show environment example; not a chassis total
svg.data-air-filter: ASR-9902-FILTER, one serviceable filter on the front
svg.data-ethernet: 10-Gbps IEEE 802.3ae, 25-Gbps IEEE 802.3by and 802.3cc, 40/100-Gbps IEEE 802.3ba, 100GE PHY monitoring, IEEE 802.x flow control, full duplex, per-port byte and packet counters
svg.data-timing: 2 x BITS RJ-45, ToD RJ-45, 10 MHz and 1 PPS SMB per RP, IEEE 1588 PTP telecom profiles and SyncE
svg.data-usb: 1 x USB class A per RP
svg.data-etsi: EN300 386, ETSI 300 019 Storage 1.1, Transportation 2.3, Stationary 3.1, EN55022, EN55024, EN50082-1/EN-61000-6-1
svg.data-emc: FCC Class A, ICES 003 Class A, AS/NZS 3548 Class A, CISPR 22 (EN55022) Class A, VCCI Class A, BSMI Class A, IEC/EN 61000-3-2, IEC/EN 61000-3-3

The chassis PID is ASR-9902 either way; the supplies are separate line items.","kind":"orderable","part-numbers":{"ASR 9902 Router, DC supplies":{"part":"ASR-9902"}}}},"description":"Cisco ASR 9000 Series ASR 9902 Router - a 2 RU fixed-port aggregation services router delivering up to 800 Gbps. Two route processors across the top and the integrated fixed board below them, carrying forty-eight ports in two mirrored slices: eight SFP28, three QSFP28 and one QSFP-DD and twelve SFP+ on each. The rear carries two 1.6 kW power modules at the ends and three fan trays between them, with the power switch on the left panel and the NEBS grounding lug on the right. Airflow is front to back. Nothing seats in the front: the board is part of the chassis and there is no Port Expansion Card bay, which is what separates this from its 3 RU ASR 9903 sibling.","format":1,"gaps":[{"blocks":[],"note":"FT0, FT1 and FT2 are printed bottom-to-top on a narrow rail at the left of each tray, and the tray's own drawn plate starts on that rail rather than beside it - the captive screw sits on the same strip. This model draws each tray as a filled rectangle, so the three marks land under their bays and L21 reports them. The marks are kept where the master puts them rather than moved somewhere they would render, because moving them would put ink where the device has none. It is the same defect cisco/asr-9903's fan labels carry and the same fix closes both.","reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["rear","fan-trays"],"wanted":"cisco/asr-9902-fan@1 drawn with its left flange cut away where the chassis prints the slot label, so the mark shows through.","what":"fan-bay-labels-sit-on-the-tray-flange"},{"blocks":[],"note":"CISCO'S OWN STENCIL AND ITS OWN DATA SHEETS DISAGREE ABOUT HOW WIDE THIS CHASSIS IS RELATIVE TO ITS SIBLING. The ASR 9902 and ASR 9903 front masters draw their bodies 1568.93 and 1569.68 art units wide, the same outline to 0.2 mm, while c78-744663 gives 439.74 mm for this chassis and c78-744035 gives 443.86 mm for the 9903. THIS FILE TAKES THE 439.74 and the evidence for that choice is a ruler inside the artwork rather than a preference: at that scale the twenty SFP-class cage columns come out on a 14.253 mm pitch against SFF-8433's 14.25, while the same measurement on the ASR 9903 at its own stated width lands on 14.36, which is 0.8 percent over a standard that does not vary. So the 9902 is the chassis the outline fits. WHAT IT COSTS IF THE READING IS WRONG is about 0.9 percent on every x on this face and on the RP slot pitch, which would go from 209.58 to 211.44.","reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["front"],"wanted":"a Cisco mechanical drawing of either chassis, or a tape measure across a real ASR 9902 and a real ASR 9903 - two numbers that would settle both models at once. Tracked in roc-ops/Portrayal#374.","what":"two-chassis-one-body-outline"},{"blocks":[],"note":"THE TOP, BOTTOM AND TWO SIDES ARE SIZED AND NOT DRAWN, and each carries an `empty:` sentence saying where the search ran. What they have in common is that no source in the intake ELEVATES them. The Visio stencil's 119 masters are front and rear elevations and hold no plan or side view at all. The install guide's figures for this chassis are two elevations, a top-view FOOTPRINT (Figure 18, which dimensions the outline and draws no feature), an airflow path, eight rack-mounting sequences across 19-inch and 23-inch, 2-post and 4-post racks, a stacking figure and an air-filter view - the mounting figures show the sides at an angle and dimension nothing on them. The data sheet gives the envelope. WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE, from the photographs, is a cisco wordmark and a product label on the top, feet and bracket landings underneath, and a bracket rail on each side. None is positioned by anything, and drawing them by eye off a three-quarter render would put unmeasured furniture on four faces at once.","reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["top","bottom","left","right"],"wanted":"a Cisco mechanical drawing of the ASR 9902, or orthographic photographs of the top and one side with something of known size in frame.","what":"four-faces-carry-no-documented-feature"},{"blocks":[],"note":"The furniture strip at the right of the RP row carries a captive screw, a round dimple above it and a small dark circle between them, and the guide names none of the three. The same two unnamed features appear on the ASR 9903 in the same place. They are the right shape for an ESD wrist-strap jack and a captive-screw well, and calling them so would be a guess with a citation attached, so they are left off the face.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["front"],"wanted":"a callout in a Cisco figure, or a photograph of the front right corner close enough to read the two features.","what":"front-right-furniture-unidentified"},{"blocks":[],"note":"Ports 11 and 37 get the same four-state Port Status vocabulary as the other forty-six, out of Table 27, because Table 27 is written for a port and does not distinguish media. WHAT IS NOT SAID is whether a lamp beside a QSFP-DD running a 400G coherent module means anything different - the coherent optics section of the configuration guide describes transponder and muxponder modes and their alarms and never mentions the faceplate lamp. So the lamp says what Table 27 says it says, and nothing here claims it reports coherent state.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["qsfp-dd","port-leds"],"wanted":"a Cisco LED table written for the QSFP-DD ports on this chassis.","what":"per-port-lamp-colour-for-the-qsfp-dd-ports"}],"groups":{"board-status":{"index-origin":0,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"fan-trays":{"attrs":{"redundancy-note":"NO FORM IS STATED AND NONE IS INVENTED, so this group carries a note and no `redundancy`. The data sheet says \"3 fans in redundant configuration\" and lists \"Fan redundancy\" in Table 2 with no arithmetic beside it, and the Cisco ASR 9000 Series Fixed-Port Routers Hardware Installation Guide gives replacement steps and no ratio. It is the ruling edgecore/csr310 carries for \"Hot swappable redundant fan modules\""},"index-origin":0,"physical-context":"Fan","role":"service","term":"FT"},"grounding":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Point"},"port-leds":{"index-origin":0,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"power-modules":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"1+1","redundancy-note":"data sheet c78-744663 Table 2, twice over: \"1.6 kW DC power module (up to 2 modules), redundancy: 1+1\" and \"1.6 kW AC power module (up to 2 modules), redundancy: 1+1\". The install guide adds the constraint that decides a build: \"A total of two AC or DC power supplies are allowed in the Cisco ASR 9902 chassis\", and mixing AC and DC is not supported"},"index-origin":0,"physical-context":"Power Module","role":"service","term":"PM"},"power-switch":{"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"Switch"},"qsfp-dd":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp-dd","speed":"100g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"qsfp28":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp28","speed":"100g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"rp-slots":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"1+1","redundancy-note":"the Cisco ASR 9000 Series Fixed-Port Routers Hardware Installation Guide lists \"Route Processors (RPs) | A99-RP-F | 2\" in its ASR 9902 components table, and the data sheet c78-744663 says the router \"supports two redundant Route Processors (RPs)\" and lists \"Route processor redundancy\" in Table 2. NEITHER NAMES A FORM, and 1+1 is the reading: with exactly two slots and redundancy between them there is no other arithmetic"},"index-origin":0,"physical-context":"NetworkingDevice","role":"management","term":"RP"},"sfp-plus":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp-plus","speed":"10g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"sfp28":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp28","speed":"25g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"Cisco","maturity":"modelled","model":"ASR 9902","name":"asr-9902","portfolio":{"family":"Aggregation Services Router","line":"Service Provider","series":"ASR 9000 Series"},"profile":"networking","provenance":{"air-filter":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"NOT DRAWN, deliberately, and for the reason the ASR 9903's is not: ASR-9902-FILTER mounts on the FRONT of the chassis, in front of every face this model draws - Figure 178, \"Install Air Filter-Cisco ASR 9902\", shows it sliding onto the front mounting brackets as a full-face frame. Drawing it would hide the whole front view, and it is an option rather than part of the chassis. ASR-9902-CAB-MGMT is left out for the reason the modelling guide gives for cable management generally: it is not a panel fact."},"chassis":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - Table 2 of c78-744663, \"Physical dimensions (includes ejector bracket/lever); (H x W x D); weight\": ASR 9902 chassis with 2 RPs, 2 PSUs and 3 FANs, 3.45 x 17.3 x 19 in. and 46.39 lb, or 87.63 x 439.74 x 482.60 mm and 21.04 kg. THE DEPTH NOTE IS A TAUTOLOGY AND IS NOT A SECOND FIGURE. Underneath the row Cisco writes \"Note: Excluding ejector, the depth is 19 in./482.6 mm\" - the same number the row already gives, so unlike the ASR 9903, where the two differ by 162 mm, there is nothing here to choose between. The data sheet's own overview agrees a third time: \"The compact size (depth is 19 in., 483 mm)\". So `chassis.depth` is 482.60 and no gap is opened over it. WIDTH IS THE BODY: 439.74 mm is 17.3 in, not the 19 in rack face, so this figure is already between the ear folds and L43 has nothing to catch. HEIGHT IS THE CHASSIS AS BUILT, NOT THE RACK ALLOCATION: 87.63 mm against 2 RU's 88.90, built 1.27 mm under its allocation for clearance, the same shortfall the ASR 9903, 9904, 9906 and 9910 show. The install guide quotes the allocation instead - \"Height of the ... Cisco ASR 9902 Router is 3.45 inches (8.77 cm)\" is 87.63 and agrees, while its ASR 9903 line quotes 5.25 in, which is that chassis's 3 RU allocation rather than its height. The data sheet figure is carried and the RU is carried separately."},"cooling":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - \"3 fans in redundant configuration\", Table 2's Redundancy row lists \"Fan redundancy\" with no ratio, and Airflow is \"Front to back\". The install guide adds the filter: \"The Cisco ASR 9903 and Cisco ASR 9902 Router have a serviceable air filter (Cisco PID: ASR-9903-FILTER and ASR-9902-FILTER).\" THE REDUNDANCY RATIO IS NOT PUBLISHED AND IS NOT SUPPLIED. The group carries a `redundancy-note` and no `redundancy`, and L69 warns that this chassis does not say how many fans it can lose. Three trays described as redundant is 2+1 and nothing else worth writing - but Cisco does not write it, and the ruling edgecore/csr310 carries for \"Hot swappable redundant fan modules\" applies the same way here as it does on the ASR 9903."},"face-check":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"done BEFORE measuring, because Cisco's master filenames name the wrong faces on the ASR 9910 and nothing downstream would have caught it. No swap here. \"ASR-9902 Front\" carries the two A99-RP-F cards, the forty-eight numbered ports, the two slice bands and the CISCO / ASR 9902 branding, and matches Figure 1 of the install guide, \"Front Panel of the Cisco ASR 9902 Router\". \"ASR-9902 Rear\" carries the two power modules, the three fan trays, the power switch and the grounding lug, and matches Figure 2."},"fixed-board":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"THE FIXED BOARD IS NOT A BAY, and Cisco is in two minds about how to say so. Table 2 of the install guide lists it as a component with a part number - \"Fixed Board Line Card | ASR-9902-LC | 1\" - and the troubleshooting chapter's `show environment` gives it a slot and a power allocation, \"0/0 ASR-9902-LC 614 283 ON\". But the data sheet calls the ports \"integrated\" four times, the router \"consists of the fixed board\", and the guide's replacement chapter - which has a procedure for the RPs, the power modules, the fan trays and the air filter - has none for it. So its forty-eight ports are placements on the chassis face, and the part number and the 614 W allocation are recorded in attrs rather than on a module nobody can remove. THE NUMBERING IS THE GUIDE'S AND THE MASTER'S TOGETHER. Figure 119, \"Cisco ASR 9902 Fixed Ports\", gives the arrangement by slice - \"SFP28 ports; eight on each slice\", \"QSFP28 ports; three on each slice\", \"QSFP-DD ports; one on each slice\", \"SFP+ ports; twelve on each slice\" - and the master prints all forty-eight numerals under the cages, 0 to 23 on the blue slice-0 band and 24 to 47 on the purple slice-1 band. Eight plus four plus twelve is twenty-four a slice, and the two readings agree port for port. THE BOARD IS MIRROR-SYMMETRIC. Slice 0 runs SFP28, QSFP, SFP+ left to right and slice 1 runs SFP+, QSFP, SFP28, so the two QSFP blocks sit inboard and the two SFP28 blocks at the ends."},"grounding":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"install guide for what it is, master for where. \"Cisco ASR 9902 and Cisco ASR 9903 Router - One grounding lug, which has two M5 bolt holes\", and Figure 74, \"NEBS Bonding and Grounding Points on the Cisco ASR 9902 Router\". The rear master draws the two holes 15.95 mm apart on centres, on a lug landing at the right-hand rear panel, with an IEC 60417-5019 earth symbol below it and a hex bonding stud to its left. cisco/a9k-ground-pad@1 carries a 15.3 mm two-hole pitch, which covers it to within 0.65 mm, and it is placed unrotated here because this chassis mounts the lug flat where the ASR 9903 mounts it upright. ONE EARTH MARK, NOT TWO. cisco/a9k-ground-pad@1 draws its own IEC 60417-5019 mark beside the lug, so no separate symbol is placed here; the master puts the mark BELOW the lug instead, and that difference is the component's drawing convention rather than a second grounding point."},"port-lamps":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing for the count and the positions, install guide for the states. FORTY-EIGHT LAMPS FOR FORTY-EIGHT PORTS, one each, all on one baseline at y 82.00 and all cut to 2.78 x 1.59 mm, each beside its port's direction triangle - down for the upper port of a stacked pair, up for the lower. The rule reaches the end of the face: port 47's lamp is at 422.43 like every other, and no port on this board is without one. THE STATES ARE TABLE 27 of the install guide, \"Port Status and LC FAIL LEDs\", transcribed: Port Status LEDs, one per port: green = port up with a valid physical-layer link; blinking = line activity, the LED going green-amber-green; red = port up but link lost, or an SFP/QSFP failure; off = port administratively shut down. The blinking state is carried as a green lamp with an amber second colour, which is what \"green-amber-green\" describes."},"power":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - Table 2 of c78-744663: \"1.6 kW DC power module (up to 2 modules), redundancy: 1+1\" and \"1.6 kW AC power module (up to 2 modules), redundancy: 1+1\", with \"Mixing of AC and DC modules is not supported\". The install guide adds the input ranges, shared with the ASR 9903 because it is the same module: 200-240 V high line and 90-130 V low line for AC, -48 VDC nominal over a -40.5 to -72 V range at 40 A maximum for DC. THE ONE PER-FRU TABLE IN THE INTAKE WAS TAKEN ON THIS CHASSIS. The troubleshooting chapter's `show environment` example is an ASR 9902 with two supplies and three fans, and its allocations - ASR-9902-LC 614 W, A99-RP-F 102 W, ASR-9902-FAN 72 W - are this chassis's own rather than a sibling's. That is why cisco/asr-9902-fan@1 carries a power figure and cisco/asr-9903-fan@1 does not. THE CHASSIS CARRIES NO ENVELOPE FIGURE AND THIS FILE INVENTS NONE. Neither document states a typical or maximum chassis draw, so there is no power-max-w here and the per-module figures stand on their own."},"power-switch":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"IT IS A REAL SWITCH AND THE GUIDE NAMES IT, which is the difference between this chassis and its sibling. Figure 154, \"Power Switch on the Cisco ASR 9902 Router\", callouts: \"1 Power Switch, 2 Power Status\", and the step it illustrates reads \"Set the power switch to the ON position. The chassis power LED turns Red.\" The switch is the slider under the yellow ATTENTION / ON-OFF tag on the left-hand rear panel, and the Power Status lamp is the small round lens below it. IT IS DRAWN AND NOT SEATED. A panel switch is not a module, so the frame and its tag are panel decor and the legend is silkscreen; only the lamp is a placement, because a lamp is a thing the viewer lights. The lamp's POSITION is read off a 4x render of the master by eye - it is drawn as a stroked circle with no fill, which the shape parser does not carry - while its legend and its identity are the guide's. THE MASTER AND THE GUIDE DISAGREE ABOUT ONE WORD, and only one of them is printed here. Cisco's photograph prints POWER in the space under the tag with the lamp below it; the Visio master prints STATUS in that same space. They are not two legends in two places - they are one legend, worded twice. The master's word is carried, because the master is what positions every other mark on this face and printing both would put ink on the metal twice over. If a photograph of a real ASR 9902 rear settles it the other way, the change is one string."},"rp-slots":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"The two RP slots are on a 209.58 mm pitch and the bays carry that figure, while the module they accept, cisco/a99-rp-f@1, declares a 221.84 mm envelope, so L33 reports 12.26 mm on each. This is the same situation the ASR 9903 carries and the same reason: the a99-rp-f master's art includes a retention bracket at each end and its Visio shape box measures the lot, and in the chassis those brackets interleave. THE PITCH IS THE DRAWING'S, TWENTY-ONE TIMES OVER. Every feature of RP1 sits exactly 209.58 mm left of its twin on RP2 - the yellow A99-RP-F band at 20.30 against 229.88, SYNC0 at 63.07 against 272.64, and nineteen more - and the two plates measure 220.21 mm each, overlapping by 10.63. IT IS NOT THE SAME NUMBER AS THE ASR 9903'S 211.44 AND THE DIFFERENCE IS NOT PHYSICAL. In ART UNITS the two masters place the RPs identically, at 747.73 and 747.75 units; the mm differ only because the two chassis bodies the pitch is anchored to differ by 4.12 mm. Whichever body figure is wrong - see the-stencil-draws-both-bodies-the-same-width - one of the two pitches is wrong with it, by about 0.9 percent. The bay is sized to the pitch either way, because docs/bay-and-component-size.md is explicit that a bay may exceed the opening and must never exceed the pitch."},"slices":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"install guide for what they are, master for where they are. \"The 48 ports are grouped in slice 0 and slice 1. The slice 0 is color coded in blue, and slice 1 in purple\", with the note that \"A slice is a logical grouping of physical ports\". The master paints them: a #00b0f0 band from 21.86 to 218.69 under ports 0 to 23 and a #cc66ff band from 226.40 to 425.33 under 24 to 47, each carrying its ports' numerals in white and the rate chips 10/25G, 100G and 10G in black. THE SLICE IS WHERE PORT MODE IS SET, which is why the band is worth drawing rather than treating as decoration: \"The port mode configuration is per slice and not per port\", and the configuration guide's Table 41 gives five options per slice, from the default 1x100GE, 1x100GE, 10x10GE, 10x10GE through to four-by-25GE mixes."},"sources":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"the Cisco ASR 9902 Compact High-Performance Router Data Sheet (c78-744663, 2021); the Cisco ASR 9000 Series Fixed-Port Routers Hardware Installation Guide (b-asr9001-hardware-installation-guide.pdf, last modified 2021-07-30, which despite its filename covers the 9001, 9901, 9902 and 9903); the Interface and Hardware Component Configuration Guide, IOS XR 24.x, whose Table 19 is what settles which two ports are the QSFP-DDs; and Cisco's own Visio stencil Routers-Cisco_ASR_9000, masters \"ASR-9902 Front\" and \"ASR-9902 Rear\"."},"stack-orientation":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 4 QSFP pairs (port-8/port-9 to port-38/port-39), the 20 SFP pairs (port-0/port-1 to port-46/port-47)."},"stencil-calibration":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"THE TWO MASTERS CALIBRATE SEPARATELY AND THEY HAD TO BE, because their shape boxes use different conventions: \"ASR-9902 Front\" reads 1.9 x 0.35 in at 1:10, which is 482.60 x 88.90 mm - the 19 in rack face by the 2 RU ALLOCATION - while \"ASR-9902 Rear\" reads 482.60 x 87.38, which is the rack face by the CHASSIS AS BUILT to within a quarter of a millimetre. One stencil, one chassis, two conventions; the metrology note's rule that a master's height must be checked against a document every time is what caught it. Both are uniform enough to measure: x against y comes out 0.24 percent apart on the front and 0.29 on the rear, against 0.66 on the ASR 9001 and 0.06 on the ASR 9904. THE MODEL IS ANCHORED ON THE DATA SHEET BODY on both faces, because the body is what the views are: the front's ink spans 1568.93 x 315.59 art units between the ear folds and the rear's 1562.93 x 309.49, and setting each to 439.74 x 87.63 gives kx/ky of 0.280280/0.277670 and 0.281356/0.283143. THE RULER THAT CONFIRMS IT IS INSIDE THE ARTWORK. The fixed board's twenty SFP-class cage columns sit on a measured 50.85 art-unit pitch, constant to 0.01 over five consecutive gaps; at this scale that is 14.253 mm against SFF-8433's 14.25 for a ganged SFP+ assembly - 0.02 percent, on a dimension that was never an input. The cage bores then come out 9.49 x 3.53 mm and the QSFP bores 18.86 x 8.83, against 9.58 x 3.56 and 19.02 x 8.92 measured the same way on the ASR 9903: the same parts, agreeing to a percent across two chassis."},"the-stencil-draws-both-bodies-the-same-width":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ANYONE RE-MEASURES EITHER CHASSIS. The ASR 9902 and ASR 9903 front masters draw their chassis bodies 1568.93 and 1569.68 art units wide - the same outline to 0.2 mm - while Cisco publishes 439.74 mm for this chassis and 443.86 for the 9903, which is 4.12 mm apart. Both cannot be right about the drawing. THE SFP RULER SAYS THIS ONE IS THE HONEST FIT. Anchored on 439.74 the cage pitch lands on 14.253 mm against the standard's 14.25; anchored on 443.86 the ASR 9903's equivalent pitch lands on 14.36, which is 0.8 percent over a standard that does not vary. The likeliest reading is that one body outline was drawn for one of the two chassis and reused for the other, and that the ASR 9903's ports are drawn about 0.8 percent wide as a result. NOTHING IS CHANGED ON THE STRENGTH OF THAT HERE. Ports 11 and 37 are the two front-panel ports that take a QSFP-DD coherent module, which is one per slice and exactly what Figure 119's callout 5 says there should be. THE DRAWING AGREES WITHOUT BEING ASKED. On the master, the EMI gasket between the two bores of the cage holding ports 10 and 11 is drawn as a hex mesh where every other stacked cage on the board has a slotted grid, and the same is true of the cage holding 36 and 37.
